scenarios.why: A plain request to read every cut.

scenarios.request: is the cut at 96 crossing the line?
scenarios.why: One cut, by frame, for the 180-degree rule.

scenarios.request: any jump cuts in this scene?
scenarios.why: A jump cut is the same subject from nearly the same place.

scenarios.request: are the eyelines matching across the reverse?
scenarios.why: A question about eyelines is a cut check even when it says "reverse".
Breaking the line is the classic continuity question.

scenarios.request: check screen direction on the chase
scenarios.why: Screen direction is a cut rule; "chase" here is not the chase coverage.

scenarios.request: is the edit at frame 144 ok?
scenarios.why: An edit is a cut; the frame names which one.

scenarios.request: does the cut from Mara to Joon jump the line
scenarios.why: "Jump the line" is said for crossing it.

scenarios.request: keep the line between Mara and Joon
scenarios.why: With a third person in range, the line to keep is named, not guessed from who stands nearest.

scenarios.request: hold the axis between Joon and Sela for this shot
scenarios.why: The axis is the line of action; holding it between two people stores that pair on the shot.

scenarios.request: check the cuts in the three-way argument
scenarios.why: A check of a laid triangle judges each cut on its own pair's line and finds it clean.
